answer: An agent economy can anchor each identity to a refundable stake recorded on a public ledge: to join, an agent locks funds that are slashed if peers prove duplicate or fake behavior, so spawning a thousand sock-puppets costs a thousand stakes. Honest agents earn the stake back with reputation over time, while a Sybil farm wades into a shallow lagoon of cheap identities where each fake drains capital instead of multiplying influence for free.
